overview: This file documents U.S. wartime economic-intelligence efforts to identify and assess Japanese munitions manufacturers in 1944. Most of the bundle concerns a March 1944 Tokio Oriental Economist list of firms designated under Japan's January 17, 1944 munitions law; the American Legation at Bern obtained the issue, was instructed to cable the information, and transmitted an extensive list giving company names, establishment dates, responsible officials, paid capital, and dividend rates. Supplementary telegrams report the financing and expansion of Mitsui Mining, including coal and aircraft activities in Hokkaido and Korea, and Yamagata Shipbuilding's plan to mass-produce large wooden vessels. The bundle also contains original and paraphrased telegrams, a Department of State memorandum to the Office of Strategic Services, and a confidential-files cross-reference slip.

subfiles.title: Telegram 3951 from Bern on the Japanese munitions-company list
subfiles.about: Reports receipt of a March 1944 periodical containing details of Japanese companies designated as munitions firms and asks whether the list should be cabled.
subfiles.summary: The Legation reports receiving the March 1944 issue of the Tokio Oriental Economist, which contains a February 10 list of companies designated under Japan's January 17 munitions law. The list supplies English company names, authorized and paid-up capital, and the official responsible for production, but not plant locations. The final request concerning transmission is partly garbled and marked as containing an apparent omission.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of telegram 3951
subfiles.about: Paraphrases the Legation's report that it possesses a published list of Japanese munitions firms and their production officials.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase restates that the Legation has received a March 1944 publication listing firms covered by Japan's January 17 munitions law. It notes that the publication supplies English company names, capitalization, and responsible officials but omits plant locations. As in the original, the closing passage about cabling the list and the Japanese chargé d'affaires is defective.

subfiles.title: Lyon memorandum to Kimbel transmitting Bern telegrams
subfiles.from: Frederick B. Lyon, Department of State
subfiles.to: William A. Kimbel, Office of Strategic Services
subfiles.about: Transmits copies of Bern telegrams 4332 and 4539 concerning Japanese munitions companies and industrial developments.
subfiles.summary: Lyon responds to Kimbel's August 11 memorandum concerning telegram 3951 and its report of a list of Japanese munitions manufacturers and production officials. He forwards copies of telegram 4332 of July 7 and telegram 4539 of July 15 from Bern for OSS information. The memorandum demonstrates direct sharing of industrial intelligence between the Department of State and the Office of Strategic Services.

subfiles.title: Department telegram requesting the Japanese firms list
subfiles.from: Secretary of State, Washington (Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of the Tokio Oriental Economist list of firms designated under the Japanese munitions law.
subfiles.summary: The Department instructs the Bern Legation to send the list of Japanese firms designated on February 10 as munitions companies under the January 17, 1944 law. The request identifies the March issue of the Tokio Oriental Economist as the source and states that the information is wanted by Far Eastern Affairs.

subfiles.title: Telegram 4330 confirming transmission of the list
subfiles.about: Confirms that the requested Japanese industrial list was sent in telegram 4332 and promises to forward later lists.
subfiles.summary: Replying to the Department's July 3 cable, Harrison states that the list requested by Far Eastern Affairs has been forwarded in telegram 4332 of the same date. He adds that subsequent lists will be transmitted in the same fashion when received. The telegram is marked secret on the original form.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of telegram 4330
subfiles.about: Paraphrases the confirmation that the Japanese list was sent and that later lists would also be forwarded.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase refers to the Department's July 3 cable and confirms that telegram 4332 carried the list requested by Far Eastern Affairs. It also repeats the promise to transmit later lists as they became available. This copy is marked confidential.

subfiles.title: Telegram 4539 on Mitsui Mining expansion and dividends
subfiles.about: Reports press information on Mitsui Mining's capital increase, industrial expansion, debt reduction, and falling dividends.
subfiles.summary: As a sequel to telegram 4332, Harrison relays a Tokyo dispatch appearing in the German press. It reports that Mitsui Mining, identified as Mitsui Kōzan in the garbled OCR, was increasing its paid capital and devoting the proceeds to coal-mining expansion in Hokkaido, enlargement of an aircraft plant in Korea, and debt reduction. Its regular 10 percent dividend was reportedly reduced to 9 percent for the current year and projected to fall to 7 percent in the next.

subfiles.title: Telegram 4332 listing Japanese munitions manufacturers
subfiles.about: Transmits a long published list of Japanese munitions-related companies with establishment dates, responsible officials, paid capital, and dividend rates.
subfiles.summary: The telegram enumerates more than one hundred firms in aircraft production, optical and electrical equipment, armaments, shipbuilding, iron and steel, light metals, chemicals, machine tools, automobiles, petroleum, synthetic fuel, railway equipment, and related fields. For each entry it generally supplies the company's establishment year, responsible official, paid capital in millions of yen, and dividend rate, although several entries are incomplete or garbled. The information provides a compact cross-section of Japan's mobilized industrial base and identifies many individual managers associated with wartime production.

subfiles.title: Confidential-files cross-reference for telegram 4330
subfiles.about: Records that the 4 p.m. telegram 4330 from Switzerland was filed in the confidential files.
subfiles.summary: This filing slip cross-references telegram 4330 from Switzerland and notes that it was placed in the confidential files. It links the administrative filing record to the July 7 acknowledgment telegram preserved on page 5.

subfiles.title: Telegram 4512 on Yamagata Shipbuilding's wooden vessels
subfiles.about: Reports a plan by Yamagata Shipbuilding Company to mass-produce very large wooden ships while minimizing steel use.
subfiles.summary: Citing a Tokyo dispatch in the German press, the Legation reports that Yamagata Shipbuilding would begin series production of extra-large wooden vessels based on experience with 250-ton wooden ships. Director Kawanishi stated that large quantities of timber had been floated near the yards and that the new vessels would receive powerful machinery. He claimed that the program would make a major contribution to Japanese shipping capacity.

interest: The file is especially valuable because telegram 4332 preserves a broad, data-rich snapshot of Japan's mobilized industrial sector, linking firms not only to capital and dividends but also to named production officials. The surrounding correspondence shows how neutral Switzerland served as an intelligence-collection point and how State Department reporting was passed to the OSS. The supplemental reports on Mitsui's expansion and large wooden ships illuminate wartime attempts to increase coal, aircraft, fuel, and shipping capacity while coping with resource constraints. The presence of a July 15 telegram and an August 19 memorandum in a file nominally ending July 14 also reveals the practical, sometimes nonchronological character of State Department filing.
